quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle takes longer to stop on wet or icy roads. Stopping also takes longer on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: When you drive where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and may run out in front of you without looking.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain because water brings oil from the road surface up to the top. This is worse in hot weather, when heat and water cause more oil to rise.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first when entering the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: Driving at night requires extra care because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well as during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when objects are not visible for 500 feet, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: An approaching driver's high beams are not dimmed. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the headlights and lets you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: If traffic lights at an intersection are not working due to a power outage:

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers your plans.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then proceed carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to come to a complete stop.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians go, and only move when it is safe.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Both directions can pass.
No one can pass.
You can pass if you are at the top of a hill.
You can pass during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is going the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen carefully at railroad tracks. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the rails.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Makes drivers react slower to hazards.
Usually makes drivers go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes drivers react slower to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol on public roads. You cannot have an open alcohol container in any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on cloudy days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an approaching car or within 500 feet of a car you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left or when passing pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders if the opposite lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night:

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use only parking lights.
Use only headlights.
Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Typical driving speeds for the area
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum or minimum speed for that road. These limits apply in ideal conditions. You must drive slower when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to avoid driving next to it.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass it quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to avoid driving next to it.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at emergency scenes.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal means the same thing as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, you should:

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car. People are most likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car. People are most likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers will find you more easily if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Warning signals include flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger, or a train horn. Do not drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: A loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak allows these gases to enter the car. To stay safe, fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before you drink that you will not drive.
Saying no if someone offers you a drink while you are driving.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after you have been drinking.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers in that lane which direction they must go. Drivers must follow traffic signals and signs before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Grip the steering wheel tightly and slowly stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and slowly stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard if your tire blows out. Hold the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by letting off the gas. Once you are going very slowly, brake lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: If you see this sign, what should you do?

options.text: You must not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. Drivers must obey all regulatory signs. This sign means passing other vehicles is not allowed in this area.
